title: ASSESSMENT OF THE ANTIFUNGAL ACTIVITY OF NYSTATIN AND OTHER ANTIFUNGAL AGENTS AGAINST CANDIDA SPECIES USING A MICRODILUTION METHOD TO DETERMINE MINIMUM INHIBITORY CONCENTRATIONS IN ACCORDANCE WITH EUCAST
summary:
Participation in the study is completed after a single appointment.
The patient visits the gynaecologist’s surgery due to current symptoms (itching, burning, changes in vaginal discharge). Once the doctor has diagnosed a ‘vaginal yeast infection’, the patient is asked if she would like to take part in the study.
The patient is given a detailed explanation of the purpose and procedure of the study. Upon giving written consent to participate in the study, an additional swab is taken from the vagina. The procedure is similar to a routine gynaecological examination and causes no significant pain. The swab is then sent to a laboratory for further analysis to determine the type of yeast and any possible resistance.
The doctor documents previous treatments and any potential risk factors. All information is recorded in such a way that no conclusions can be drawn about the identity of the participant. There is no additional time commitment or disadvantage for participants. Participation takes place as part of the normal clinic visit, and treatment remains unaffected.

interventions.name: In the study, the intervention consists of an additional, one-off vaginal swab taken from adult women diagnosed with vulvovaginal candidiasis. This is a one-off procedure for each patient, taking less than a minute.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Women aged 18 years and over
•    Acute and/or chronic recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis
•    Confirmed diagnosis of vulvovaginal candidiasis in accordance with the guideline (AWMF 015/072) (medical history, clinical presentation, unstained smear)
Exclusion criteria:
•    Females under 18 years of age
•    Other gynaecological infections other than vulvovaginal candidiasis (e.g. bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis or similar)
•    Current treatment with antifungal or antibiotic medication for infections of the external and/or internal genital area
